---
title: "Session 14 guided lab"
subtitle: "Estimate Type I error and power"
---

Copy `starter/simulation-lab.qmd` to `work/session14/`.

::: {.callout-note}
**Suggested use:** Tasks 1–7 are the core Type-I-error and power study.
Additional practice expands the same ADEMP study to bias, coverage, sample size,
and two additional data-generating mechanisms. Remaining scenarios may be run
independently after lab.
:::

## Tasks

1. Write an ADEMP specification for comparing Welch's t test with the equal-
   variance t test when group variances differ.
2. Complete `simulate_one()` and verify one replicate by inspecting its generated
   data and returned values.
3. Run both methods under the null and estimate Type I error.
4. Run at two nonzero mean differences and estimate power.
5. Report Monte Carlo SE for every rejection probability.
6. Count failed/nonfinite replicates and retain the condition parameters.
7. Increase the replicate count until the worst MCSE meets a precision target you
   state in advance.

## Additional practice: broaden the ADEMP study

1. Extend one simulation replicate so that each method returns the estimate,
   estimated standard error, 95% confidence interval, and p-value.
2. Add bias, empirical SD, mean estimated SE, coverage, and mean interval width
   to the performance summary.
3. Repeat selected null and alternative scenarios for group sizes 15, 30, and
   100. Keep the variance ratio unchanged.
4. Add a centered, variance-standardized log-normal error distribution. State
   its true mean and variance in the ADEMP specification.
5. Add a rare-outlier mechanism and retain the number of injected outliers in
   each replicate rather than silently discarding unusual samples.
6. Build one scenario table containing the data-generating mechanism, sample
   size, effect, replicate count, seed, and target precision.
7. Make one diagnostic figure that helps compare performance across sample sizes
   or data-generating mechanisms. Include Monte Carlo uncertainty where useful.
8. Mark which conclusions appear stable and which require more replicates or a
   wider scenario grid.

### Independent-practice check

The true estimand must be explicit in every scenario. Coverage is the proportion
of intervals containing that truth—not the proportion containing the observed
estimate from a single generated dataset.

## Exit evidence

Render ADEMP, tested function, scenario table, Monte Carlo uncertainty, failure
count, and interpretation. Do not claim that simulation proves a method is
universally valid.
